title: US markets closed — Labor Day (compresses the September coupon block into a four-session week — the instance immediately after 2026, not 2031)
source: NEWS: TWO INDUSTRY PRIMARIES, both fetched direct by THIS session 2026-09-06 rather than inherited from the proposal this file supersedes. (1) nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars (HTTP 200, 109,180 bytes): the page states "All NYSE markets observe U.S. holidays as listed below for 2026, 2027, and 2028" and its Labor Day row reads across those three columns verbatim as "Monday, September 7 | Monday, September 6 | Monday, September 4" -- so the 2027 column is 2027-09-06, a full closure. The same page's four early-close disclaimers were read in full and name ONLY Monday July 3 2028, the day after Thanksgiving (Friday November 27 2026, Friday November 26 2027, Friday November 24 2028) and Thursday December 24 2026: NYSE lists no early close in September of any year it covers. (2) sifma.org/resources/general/holiday-schedule (HTTP 200, 298,899 bytes), read out of the page's own embedded payload: its 2027 US panel renders heading "Labor Day", date "Monday, September 6, 2027", note EMPTY -- a full fixed-income close with no recommended early close on the preceding Friday -- and the string "September 3, 2027" appears ZERO times on the page. THE EMPTY NOTE WAS VERIFIED AS MEANINGFUL RATHER THAN A PARSING ARTIFACT: the same extractor on the same fetch returns non-empty notes for the 2027 entries that do carry one, "Good Friday | Friday, March 26, 2027 | Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Thursday, March 25, 2027" and "Memorial Day | Monday, May 31, 2027 | Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Friday, May 28, 2027". Independently reproduced by statute and weekday arithmetic: 5 U.S.C. 6103 fixes Labor Day on the FIRST Monday in September, and the first Monday of September 2027 is 2027-09-06. Filed estimate on the same three counts every sibling closure entry documented (labor-day-market-closure-2026-09-07, memorial-day-market-closure-2027-05-31, good-friday-market-closure-2027-03-26, presidents-day-market-closure-2027-02-15): the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an exchange's or a trade association's own holiday calendar, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and the proposal this file promotes was estimate by contract. The DATE is not in doubt -- the estimate label is about the taxonomy, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-06 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, promoting the single proposal proposals/labor-day-market-closure-2027-09-06.from-fomc-blackout-start-2027-09-04.json (read in full first; no competing proposal existed). The proposal's framing was the FOMC blackout -- correct but already owned and already REFUSED upstream by fomc-blackout-start-2027-09-04, which measured Labor Day inside the gate as routine (5 of 21 September gates) and an 8-session gate as routine (4 of 19). THE TITLE MOVED TO WHAT THE RESEARCH ACTUALLY FOUND, and it is a correction to a sibling: labor-day-market-closure-2026-09-07 states the compressed-coupon-week structure 'returns on the same rule -- Labor Day on Sep 6 or 7 -- next in 2031 and 2032'. Computed cold this session for 1993-2040, 2031's Labor Day is SEPTEMBER 1, so 2031 is not a compressed year at all, and the true next instance is 2027 -- THIS event, 12 months after the sibling and not 5 years. The compressed set 2009-2040 is 2009, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2021, 2026, 2027, 2032, 2037, 2038. VALIDATED AGAINST TREASURY'S OWN RECORD, 6 of 6: in every Labor-Day-on-Sep-6-or-7 year the 3-Year note prices on the Tuesday immediately after the holiday (2009-09-08, 2010-09-07, 2015-09-08, 2020-09-08, 2021-09-07, 2026-09-08) with the 10Y and 30Y on the Wednesday and Thursday, where in all 12 non-compressed years the block lands 2027-09-09 to 09-12, i.e. the FOLLOWING week -- so 2027's block projects to Tue 09-07 / Wed 09-08 / Thu 09-09 (api.fiscaldata.treasury.gov auctions_query, 6,020 rows 2009-01-05 to 2026-09-10, fetched HTTP 200 this session). AND THE COMPRESSION'S HEADLINE IS MOSTLY NOT COMPRESSION: the Tuesday-after-Labor-Day stack runs 1.77x a same-year median Tuesday in the TWELVE NON-compressed years against 2.11x in the six compressed ones, and the coupon leg was $58B of 2026-09-08's $304B (19%) -- the displaced Monday bill slate is a Monday-holiday effect that fires every Labor Day, and compression adds one coupon on top. IMPACT LOW AND STRUCTURAL ONLY: a closed session moves nothing by itself and no house playbook is calendar-keyed (docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md re-grepped this session for 'holiday|labor day|closure|half-day|early close': 0 and 0). It widens caution and licenses nothing. HONEST LIMIT ON THE KIND FIELD: EventKind (src/domain/market-events-types.ts) has no market-structure member, so this is filed 'sector', the same least-wrong choice every sibling closure entry documented. DUPLICATE CHECK RUN: the calendar carried a Labor Day entry for 2026 only, no canonical labor-day-market-closure-2027-09-06.json existed, and exactly one proposal for this id existed.
